To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
morphogen signaling proteins transfer from producing cells to neighboring target cells at the sites of direct cell-cell contact.
morphogen signaling proteins transfer from producing cells to target cells at the interface of direct cell-cell contact, even when these cells are not immediate cell neighbors.
morphogens disperse by direct transfer from producing to receiving cells at points of contact, even when producing and receiving cells are not immediate developmental neighbors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how morphogen signaling molecules disperse across developmental tissues.
the physical and chemical mechanisms that control morphogen distribution and signaling.
the mechanisms by which cells communicate with one another in developing tissues.

morphogen proteins are directly transferred from producing to target tissues at points of cell-cell contact.
the mechanisms that generate the steady-state distributions and the morphogen gradients are not well understood.
the morphogen distribution is determined by the direct transfer of signaling proteins between cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
morphogens disperse by direct delivery mechanisms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of morphogens across developmental fields is a direct result of the spatial organization of the tissues in which they are expressed.
morphogens are not simply secreted into the extracellular space, but are instead actively transferred from cell to cell.
morphogens can disperse across developmental spaces through direct transfer between cells, rather than through diffusion in the extracellular fluid.
